key_insight: Destructive many-photon interference can suppress false heralding from detector loss and noise, improving photonic entangled-state quality beyond what fidelity alone reveals.
engineering_relevance: Error-aware seed-state design could improve the reliability of photonic quantum computing without focusing solely on resource count or generation success probability.
method: Develop a framework that separates sensitivities to physically distinct linear-optical errors.
Identify seed-state generators where interference blocks detector-induced false-success events.
Design Bell-state and four-qubit GHZ-state generators with improved error or success performance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports halved effective output loss for particular Bell-state generators versus a standard scheme, a new Bell generator insensitive to detector loss and noise to first order, and a four-qubit GHZ generator with over 75% higher success probability than a standard circuit.
watch_item: First-order protection does not establish immunity to higher-order errors, and the abstract does not report experimental validation.
paper_title: Beyond Fidelity: Resolving Errors in Photonic Seed State Generation
